memory_update.text: HSTM should remain a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the credential_assessment_compliance_layer because it combines healthcare workforce learning, compliance, continuing education, certification tracking, and credentialing/privileging SaaS.
FA is a second-order but node-relevant underfollowed candidate: education and credential verification may be buried inside broader employment screening and compliance workflows.
GHC/Kaplan provides direct exposure to licensure and certification prep, but exposure purity is diluted by the holding-company structure and non-education segments.
The strongest direct public exposures for this node may not screen as education stocks; they may sit in healthcare SaaS, HR verification, information services, or conglomerate education segments.

Private companies dominate several subnodes, including Prometric, ETS, Ascend Learning, UWorld, Meazure Learning, and Proctorio; public-market exposure may require indirect plays or diluted conglomerates.

HSTM should be promoted for deeper Layer 2 research as the cleanest underfollowed public exposure to healthcare credentialing, CE compliance, provider privileging, and regulated workforce record systems.
GHC/Kaplan is a hidden professional licensure and certification prep candidate, but purity is diluted by Graham Holdings' diversified asset base; verify Kaplan segment contribution before ranking.

FA is a second-order credential-verification play, not an education provider; include only if later evidence shows education / license / credential verification is material or growing inside screening workflows.

Pearson remains the reference benchmark for assessment scale, proctoring, test security, biometric identity, and certification / licensure exam delivery; use it to define the chokepoint KPIs smaller companies should be tested against.

Several important private chokepoint vendors surfaced but were not included because the mandate is US-listed companies: Prometric, Meazure Learning / ProctorU, Proctorio, Caveon, Ascend Learning, BenchPrep, Colibri, Laerdal, and Gaumard. These may still matter as customer / competitor context.

HSTM is the cleanest underfollowed small-cap candidate for the credential_assessment_compliance_layer because it directly maps to healthcare learning, credentialing, provider verification, and compliance record systems.
GHC offers a hidden Kaplan route into test prep, professional licensure, and continuing education, but the exposure must be checked for materiality inside the diversified parent.

FA is a second-order verification gate for education-to-employment outcomes through background screening, education/work verification, credential checks, healthcare credentials, and ongoing compliance monitoring.

Many direct assessment/proctoring assets in this node appear private or foreign-listed, including exam administration, online proctoring, and standardized testing operators; US-listed discovery should therefore include adjacent verification and regulated workforce-compliance vendors.

For later layers, separate direct exam ownership/licensure prep from compliance-record infrastructure and employer verification, because these have different cyclicality, pricing power, and defensibility.
HSTM should be carried forward as the cleanest underfollowed pure-play candidate for healthcare workforce credentialing, compliance learning, and provider credentialing software.

ATGE is not a credentialing vendor, but it is a licensure-linked healthcare education operator whose value proposition depends on regulated career outcomes; carry forward as an adjacent regulated-outcomes candidate.

STRA is an adjacent employer-workforce education platform candidate; the key verification question is whether Workforce Edge and Sophia create durable verified-credit / employer-ROI infrastructure rather than generic online education exposure.
Pearson / PSO is the reference benchmark for high-stakes assessment and professional certification delivery, useful for mapping smaller credentialing and compliance software suppliers.

Further searches should target proctoring vendors, background / license verification vendors, nursing exam-prep providers, continuing-education compliance systems, and private-to-public supplier dependencies; many may be embedded inside HR tech, healthcare SaaS, or information-services labels.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the credentialing, assessment, licensure-prep, proctoring, and compliance-data node. The cleanest reference leader is Pearson via Pearson VUE, while the underfollowed lane surfaces HealthStream for healthcare credentialing and continuing-education compliance, First Advantage for credential/education/work-history verification infrastructure, and Graham Holdings via Kaplan for test prep, professional licensure, certification, and continuing education. These are research candidates only, not investment recommendations. Expanded the credentialing / assessment / compliance-data supply-chain node into a compact two-lane universe. Reference lane: Pearson is the clearest public-market anchor for high-stakes professional assessment and proctoring infrastructure. Underfollowed lane: HealthStream, Graham Holdings, and First Advantage map to narrower chokepoints around healthcare credentialing / CE compliance, professional licensure prep, and employer-side education / credential verification. The strongest chokepoint fit in this pass is HealthStream because its products sit inside regulated healthcare workforce credentialing and compliance workflows rather than broad discretionary education demand. Layer 1B expansion for the underfollowed credentialing / assessment / compliance node found a cleaner small-mid cap lane in healthcare workforce compliance, professional licensure prep, employment/education verification, and career-certification infrastructure.
